business_problem: Rio Tinto wanted AI and advanced analytics solutions that help operating teams work more safely and efficiently, and it needed a fast way to support its Annual Planning Review workshop with better access to organizational knowledge.
solution_summary: Rio Tinto’s Data & Analytics team built and deployed an internal GPT-like knowledge agent for the company’s Annual Planning Review workshop. The implementation was led by a senior data scientist and used generative AI and large language models as the core reasoning layer for the assistant. Based on the source, the agent was created to help workshop participants access and use relevant knowledge more effectively during planning activities, while supporting the company’s broader objective of safer and more efficient operations. The work was delivered through cross-team collaboration and shipped in only three weeks, enabled by technical groundwork completed in prior months. The source does not name external vendors, hosting platforms, storage systems, or integrations, so the documented architecture is limited to the internal knowledge agent, the LLM-driven processing layer, and its use in the planning workshop context.

solution_components.role: An internal knowledge assistant built for the Annual Planning Review workshop to help users access and apply relevant information.

solution_components.name: Large Language Models (LLMs)
solution_components.role: The core model capability used to power the knowledge agent’s generative reasoning and responses.

business_outcome: Rio Tinto delivered an internal AI knowledge agent in three weeks, used it in the Annual Planning Review workshop, and reinforced senior leadership’s decision to incorporate AI into business strategies while supporting safer and more efficient operations.
